text: The production is titled "Echoes of the Agora: The Oedipus Immersion." In this innovative theater experience, the rigid proscenium arch is removed, transforming the venue into a sprawling, labyrinthine reconstruction of ancient Thebes. Spectators are not passive observers but are cast as citizens of the city, wearing simple tunics and carrying lanterns. As the protagonist, Oedipus, delivers his classical dramatic monologues, he does not stand on a raised stage but moves through the crowd, making direct eye contact and addressing specific audience members as if they are his advisors or accusers. The narrative is driven by character interactions; audience members may be handed scrolls containing clues or asked to vote on moral dilemmas that influence the pacing of the scene, blending the fatalistic tone of Greek tragedy with the agency of immersive theater.
